react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolite set (pyruvic acid, oxoglutaric acid, L-glutamic acid, phosphate, isopentenyl pyrophosphate, niacinamide, dihydrolipoate, choline, L-threonine) was analysed across three complementary paradigms: RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-direct enrichment. Two pathways achieved cross-paradigm consensus. Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism emerged as the strongest winner, attaining rank 1 in RaMP (FDR = 1.3×10⁻⁸, fold-enrichment 758), rank 0 in MetaboAnalystR KEGG (p = 0.004, hsa00260), and rank 0 in mummichog (p = 0.0047). Driver metabolites driving this consensus are L-threonine (KEGG:C00188) and choline (KEGG:C00114), both annotated as pathway members in all three outputs, with L-glutamic acid (KEGG:C00025) and dihydrolipoate (KEGG:C02147) also appearing in RaMP. A secondary cross-paradigm winner is Nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism (vitamin B3), ranked 8 in RaMP (FDR = 6.97×10⁻⁴), 1 in mummichog (p = 0.019), and 5 in MetaboAnalystR (p = 0.046, hsa00760). Niacinamide (KEGG:C00153) and L-glutamic acid are the driver compounds for this pathway. The converging signal across ORA and m/z-direct paradigms strongly implicates amino-acid and one-carbon/nitrogen metabolic reprogramming, with secondary disruption of NAD⁺ salvage through the niacinamide axis. Dihydrolipoate additionally links the primary pathway to mitochondrial oxidative metabolism, consistent with the pyruvate and oxoglutarate signals detected in the study. All five input metabolites with confirmed InChIKey first-blocks are structurally distinct with no reconciliation conflicts, confirming the observed enrichment is driven by genuine biological co-abundance rather than ID ambiguity.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolite set (pyruvic acid, oxoglutaric acid, L-glutamic acid, phosphate, isopentenyl pyrophosphate, niacinamide, dihydrolipoate, choline, L-threonine) was analysed across three complementary paradigms: RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-direct enrichment. Two pathways achieved cross-paradigm consensus. Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism emerged as the strongest winner, attaining rank 1 in RaMP (FDR = 1.3×10⁻⁸, fold-enrichment 758), rank 0 in MetaboAnalystR KEGG (p = 0.004, hsa00260), and rank 0 in mummichog (p = 0.0047). Driver metabolites driving this consensus are L-threonine (KEGG:C00188) and choline (KEGG:C00114), both annotated as pathway members in all three outputs, with L-glutamic acid (KEGG:C00025) and dihydrolipoate (KEGG:C02147) also appearing in RaMP. A secondary cross-paradigm winner is Nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism (vitamin B3), ranked 8 in RaMP (FDR = 6.97×10⁻⁴), 1 in mummichog (p = 0.019), and 5 in MetaboAnalystR (p = 0.046, hsa00760). Niacinamide (KEGG:C00153) and L-glutamic acid are the driver compounds for this pathway. The converging signal across ORA and m/z-direct paradigms strongly implicates amino-acid and one-carbon/nitrogen metabolic reprogramming, with secondary disruption of NAD⁺ salvage through the niacinamide axis. Dihydrolipoate additionally links the primary pathway to mitochondrial oxidative metabolism, consistent with the pyruvate and oxoglutarate signals detected in the study. All five input metabolites with confirmed InChIKey first-blocks are structurally distinct with no reconciliation conflicts, confirming the observed enrichment is driven by genuine biological co-abundance rather than ID ambiguity.
